name: AI_Email_Crafter
headline: WhatsApp MCP Server for Integration
short_description: WhatsApp MCP is a powerful server designed for integrating WhatsApp's messaging capabilities with your applications. Built in Go, it provides access to the WhatsApp API, enabling efficient communication and automation for businesses.
author: lharries

sections.overview:
WhatsApp MCP is a Model Context Protocol server that connects your personal WhatsApp account directly to AI agents like Claude and Cursor via the WhatsApp web multidevice API. It lets you search and read messages (text, images, videos, documents, and audio), manage contacts, and send messages to individuals or groups—all while keeping your data stored locally in a SQLite database. Messages are only sent to your LLM when you explicitly access them through tools you control. The server runs on Go and integrates with the whatsmeow library for secure local-first operation. It's ideal for teams automating customer support, message monitoring, or bulk communications without third-party intermediaries.
Automate customer support responses via WhatsApp to improve response times and customer satisfaction.
Integrate marketing campaigns with WhatsApp messaging to reach customers directly and increase engagement.
Enhance sales outreach by sending personalized messages to potential clients through WhatsApp.
Send real-time notifications to customers about order updates, promotions, or important announcements.
sections.setup:
Terminal
Copy
`claude install lharries/whatsapp-mcp`
`git clone https://github.com/lharries/whatsapp-mcp`
sections.usage:
```
Use the WhatsApp MCP server to send a personalized WhatsApp message to [PROSPECT_NAME] at [PHONE_NUMBER] with the following content: '[MESSAGE_CONTENT]'. Include a call-to-action that encourages them to [DESIRED_ACTION]. Ensure the message is concise, professional, and aligned with our sales engagement strategy. If the prospect has responded previously, reference their last interaction with: '[PERSONALIZED_REFERENCE]' to maintain context.
```
